subject.title: iOS remote pairing UX: QR crash, onboarding paste fails, Settings paste works (cellular); feedback on edge auth + mobile wss://

question: Should OpenClaw document a supported split-host public exposure pattern where browser/admin access stays behind SSO or trusted-proxy auth while a separate mobile wss hostname uses OpenClaw token plus device-pair bootstrap auth?
rationale: The remaining request defines a public Gateway exposure and mobile bootstrap trust boundary, so automation should not decide whether this deployment shape is supported or what warnings and limits it needs.

options.title: Document Split-Host Mobile Pairing
options.body: Add a security-reviewed advanced recipe that keeps Tailscale Serve as the default while documenting a dedicated mobile wss hostname, no browser SSO redirect on that host, token/device bootstrap auth, trustedProxies, and validation steps.

options.title: Keep Generic Exposure Guidance
options.body: Leave public split-host mobile pairing as operator-managed advanced setup and keep docs focused on Tailscale Serve, trusted-proxy auth, and general exposure warnings.

options.title: Defer Public wss Direction
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers decide whether public mobile pairing beyond Tailscale Serve should be a first-class supported deployment shape.

recommendation.title: Document Split-Host Mobile Pairing
recommendation.body: Add a security-reviewed advanced recipe that keeps Tailscale Serve as the default while documenting a dedicated mobile wss hostname, no browser SSO redirect on that host, token/device bootstrap auth, trustedProxies, and validation steps.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the route-list fix and current iOS remote pairing docs, and is the strongest available owner for the paired security/docs decision.
